flawed_step: Step 2: a bijection that matches vertices of equal degree must preserve adjacency and non-adjacency. This cannot be justified. Step 1 is fine: equal degree sequences give a bijection sending each vertex to one of the same degree. But degree data says nothing about which vertices are joined, so there is no reason the edges line up.
counterexample: The 6-cycle C6 and two disjoint triangles (2K3). Both have 6 vertices and degree sequence {2,2,2,2,2,2}. C6 is connected and 2K3 is not, so no adjacency-preserving bijection exists between them.
assessment_summary: The statement is false. Having the same degree sequence is necessary for two graphs to be isomorphic, but it is not enough. The proof breaks when you try to turn a degree-matching bijection into one that preserves edges. C6 and 2K3 show this: same vertex count and degree sequence, but one is connected and the other is not.
